title: docs: correct the 1.46.0 upgrade note and known limits
headline: The upgrade note now says render adds the archive block itself and that a done row needs the release check run in the project, and the known limits name the test runners in plain words.
alignment: v1.46.1 corrects the release text of build 20 (v1.46.0) after its sweep fixes; no code or rule text changes.

items.text: The 1.46.0 upgrade note told a project to add an archive block by hand and named only the verify file for a done row; render adds the block, and a done row also needs the release check run in the project.
items.before: Told to add the archive block by hand
items.after: Told render adds it, and what a done row needs

verification: The build record check and the release-notes audit pass on the new text.

decisions.decision: A patch, not an edit of the 1.46.0 record
decisions.why: The 1.46.0 record is what its tag shipped; a record change is install input, so the correction ships as its own version.

upgrading: Run install user, then install project. The next render adds an archive block after the rows block where a project has none, so done and closed rows stay in sight. Marking a row done for a release now needs `item set <id> verify <result file>`, a file holding the release check's RELEASE COMPLETE line, and that check run in the project, which logs it in the project's .git folder.
limits: The test-scope check reads the common runners (node, npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, jest, mocha, pytest, go, cargo, dotnet and the like) by name; one it does not list is not read. The pop-up check reads choice pop-ups and plan files only; a chat message is not checked. The retired-wording check reads the patterns it lists, not the same rule in other words. A done row whose release names no version (a project that ships none) needs only its verify file. The release check log is read only in a main checkout, not a worktree.
